title: Create FogOfWar manager class
description: Create a dedicated FogOfWar class to manage fog state, visibility calculations, and fog node rendering.
design:
```swift
class FogOfWar {
    private let mapWidth: Int
    private let mapHeight: Int
    private let tileSize: CGFloat
    
    // Fog states: unexplored (0), explored (1), visible (2)
    private var fogState: [[Int]]
    
    private var fogNode: SKNode
    private var fogTiles: [[SKSpriteNode?]]
    
    init(mapWidth: Int, mapHeight: Int, tileSize: CGFloat)
    
    func update(visibleFrom positions: [(CGPoint, CGFloat)]) // (position, visionRange)
    func isVisible(at position: CGPoint) -> Bool
    func isExplored(at position: CGPoint) -> Bool
}
```
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] FogOfWar class created
- [ ] Tracks unexplored, explored, and visible states per tile
- [ ] Provides visibility query methods
- [ ] Manages fog node hierarchy

title: Phase 6: Fog of War and Zoom Controls
description:
Add fog of war system and zoom controls to enhance gameplay visibility and navigation.

## Features Overview

### Zoom Controls
- iOS: Pinch-to-zoom gesture for intuitive mobile control
- macOS: Scroll wheel zoom for desktop experience
- Smooth zoom transitions with configurable min/max limits
- Camera bounds adjust dynamically with zoom level
- HUD remains readable at all zoom levels

### Fog of War
- Unexplored areas are hidden/obscured
- Vision radius around player characters (Nathaniel and Hermes)
- Enemies only visible within vision range
- Explored areas remain partially visible (greyed out)
- Real-time fog updates as characters move

## Technical Approach

### Camera System Enhancements
- Add cameraZoom property to GameScene
- Modify camera update to apply scale transformations
- Adjust camera bounds clamping for zoom levels
- Inverse-scale UI elements to maintain readability

### Fog of War System
- Create fog overlay layer (semi-transparent)
- Track visible tiles based on character positions
- Use vision range property on characters
- Optimize fog updates for performance

title: Implement macOS scroll wheel zoom
description: Override scrollWheel(with:) in GameScene for macOS to handle scroll-to-zoom.
design:
```swift
#if os(macOS)
override func scrollWheel(with event: NSEvent) {
    let zoomDelta = event.scrollingDeltaY * 0.01
    updateZoom(by: 1.0 + zoomDelta)
}
#endif
```
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Scroll up zooms in
- [ ] Scroll down zooms out
- [ ] Smooth zoom response
- [ ] Works with trackpad and mouse wheel

title: TMX tileset images not found - app crashes on launch
description:
The app loads levelone.tmx successfully but crashes because tileset images are not found. Console shows:
- SKTexture: Error loading image resource: "Assets/Maps/roughrippleearthdarktograsstileset"
- SKTexture: Error loading image resource: "Assets/Maps/treestileset"  
- SKTexture: Error loading image resource: "Assets/Maps/windmilltileset"
- SKTexture: Error loading image resource: "Assets/Maps/minetileset2"

Then crashes with: Fatal error: Index out of range in ContiguousArrayBuffer.swift:691

The tileset paths in TMX files reference Assets/Maps/*.png but these images need to be either:
1. Copied to the bundle at the correct paths, or
2. TMXRenderer updated to look for them in the correct location

title: Fix iOS landscape orientation - game renders rotated 90°
description: The game scene renders rotated 90° counter-clockwise on iOS simulator. The GameViewController sets supportedInterfaceOrientations to .landscapeRight but the view still displays in portrait orientation. Need to investigate Info.plist orientation settings and ensure proper landscape lock.
notes:
Attempted fixes:
1. Added AppDelegate.supportedInterfaceOrientationsFor returning .landscape
2. Changed GameViewController.supportedInterfaceOrientations to .landscape
3. Added INFOPLIST_KEY_UIRequiresFullScreen = YES to project
4. Added INFOPLIST_KEY_UIInterfaceOrientation = UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight

The built Info.plist correctly shows landscape-only orientations and UIRequiresFullScreen=true. However, the iOS 26 simulator appears to have a bug where it doesn't rotate the device frame for landscape-only apps. The screenshot captures show the device in portrait mode with the landscape content rendered rotated.

This may be a simulator-specific issue that works correctly on real devices or older iOS versions.
